clue.text: Queen's behind rough heavy seizing dwarf's rear — problem for Sneezy?

indicators.note: Queen's behind tells us the royal abbreviation sits at the back of the rest
seizing means the rearranged letters grab and hold the dwarf's last letter inside them
rough suggests the word heavy is roughed up into a new order
the rear of the word dwarf is its final letter

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen

explanation.surface: A heavy-handed monarch roughs up a dwarf, a puzzle for one of the seven dwarfs of Snow White.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' gives HAYEV, which 'seizing' wraps round dwarf's last letter. Sneezy is one of Snow White's seven dwarfs, the theme of this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Sneezy is a dwarf forever sneezing, and a pollen allergy is the classic cause of constant sneezing.

clue.text: Happy giving makeover to empty cottage and stable

indicators.note: a makeover remodels, so the two remaining letters of cottage are rearranged
an empty cottage has lost all its middle letters, leaving just the outer pair

parts.note: static means stable, not changing

explanation.surface: A cheerful person renovates a vacant cottage and stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves only cottage's first and last letters, and 'giving makeover to' swaps them. Happy is another of the seven dwarfs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstatic means overjoyed, the extreme of being glad.

clue.text: Tragic hero's one in mounting state

indicators.note: mounting means climbing, so in this down entry the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: King Lear is the tragic hero of Shakespeare's play; with the 's this gives LEARS
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean tragic hero ascends in a mounting crisis of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns LEARS + I upwards, giving the letters in the opposite order.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel is a nation, and a state is a sovereign country.

clue.text: Say, Jolly'? Not so — Dopey

parts.note: in colloquial speech 'he goes' means 'he says'
a Jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
less means not so much, as in less happy

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a person is jolly, and is told no, they are dopey.
explanation.walkthrough: A Jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine. Dopey is one of the seven dwarfs.
explanation.definitionFit: Gormless is British slang for dim-witted or foolish, the dwarf's character.

clue.text: Opening of top-down Muslim trade union

indicators.note: top-down tells us the top letter of this down entry is moved down to the bottom

parts.note: a Shia is a member of one of the two main branches of Islam

explanation.surface: An opening appears in a top-down Muslim trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: SHIA + TU gives SHIATU; 'top-down' moves the top letter, S, to the foot of the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiatus is a gap or break, an opening in a sequence.

clue.text: Their rise and fall, potentially revealing, reflects material wealth

definitions.text: Their rise and fall, potentially revealing, reflects material wealth

parts.words: Their rise and fall, potentially revealing, reflects material wealth
parts.note: skirt lengths go up and down with fashion, showing more leg, and a popular economic theory says they rise in boom times

explanation.walkthrough: The 'hemline index' is a folk theory that skirts get shorter when the economy is strong; 'material' hints at fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Skirt edges move up and down with fashion, and the hemline theory links their height to economic prosperity.

clue.text: Sadly, I doubt Man City can be at the moment!

definitions.text: Man City can be at the moment!

indicators.note: sadly suggests the words I doubt are sorry, broken and put back in a different order

explanation.surface: A gloomy fan doubts that rich Manchester City could ever lose a bidding war.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as 'I doubt Man City can be outbid', since the club's wealth makes it hard to beat in the transfer market.
explanation.definitionFit: To be beaten by a higher offer is the fate of rival clubs, which wealthy Manchester City rarely suffers in transfer bidding.

clue.text: Put on scarf, say, and head for Arsenal -soccer is fabulous to behold endlessly

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
fabulous suggests something fanciful, so the letters of soccer is are reinvented
endlessly means the last letter of the synonym is cut off

parts.note: to behold is to see

explanation.surface: A football fan puts on a scarf and heads for a wonderful game at Arsenal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head for' takes A from Arsenal, 'fabulous' rearranges SOCCERIS into CCESSORI, and 'endlessly' shortens SEE to SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To accessorise is to add extra items such as a scarf or jewellery to an outfit.

clue.text: How text shows solver's name on vase

parts.note: in text-message shorthand, the solver's, that is your, is written UR

explanation.surface: A text message spells out the reader's name on a vase.
explanation.definitionFit: An urn is a tall rounded vessel, a kind of vase.

clue.text: Present for RC?

explanation.surface: A gift for a Roman Catholic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the nonce' means for the present time. Read as NON-CE, the answer means not Church of England, which a Roman Catholic is.
explanation.definitionFit: The nonce is the present occasion, and a Roman Catholic is non-CE, outside the Church of England.

clue.text: Cash machine swallows one note right after another — you could lose pounds there

indicators.note: after says the swallowing machine comes after this other note

parts.note: F is a musical note too

indicators.note: swallows means the machine takes these letters inside it

parts.note: ATM, automated teller machine, is a cash machine
fa is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A cash machine eats one banknote after another, so you lose money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallows' gives ATFARM. 'Pounds' and 'note' play on money but mean weight and music.
explanation.definitionFit: A health spa where people diet to lose weight is jokingly called this.

clue.text: Islamist fighters take topless resort in 3 back

indicators.note: back means the whole sequence is read backwards

parts.note: to nab is to take or seize

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: Eilat is a Red Sea resort in Israel, the answer to 3 down

explanation.surface: Militants seize a topless beach resort in a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' cuts EILAT to ILAT; 'back' reverses NAB + ILAT. The '3' refers to the answer of 3 down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taliban are an armed Afghan religious movement, fundamentalist militants.

clue.text: What makes ants' lives animated?

indicators.note: animated suggests the letters of ants' lives are set moving into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about what gives busy ants their liveliness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'animated' rearranges ANTS LIVES; the whole clue also asks what gives life its energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitalness is the quality of being full of life, which is what makes anything lively.

clue.text: Push new-sounding central idea enthralling government

indicators.note: new-sounding means a word that sounds like new, the Greek letter nu

parts.note: the word new is what is heard

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the centre of idea holds the government letter
central picks the middle letters of idea

explanation.surface: Someone pushes a fresh-sounding central idea that captivates the government.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek letter nu is said like new. 'central' takes the middle of idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudge is a gentle push or prod.

clue.text: It's said paella's made with this poison

indicators.note: it's said tells us the words are heard aloud rather than read

parts.note: paella is made with rice in it, giving the spoken phrase rice in

explanation.surface: A Spanish rice dish is made with a deadly poison.
explanation.walkthrough: Paella is a Spanish rice dish, so it is made with 'rice in', which spoken aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricin is a deadly toxin extracted from castor beans.

clue.text: Northern listeners viewed sound as far from middle-of-the-road

parts.note: ears are what we listen with

indicators.note: sound means a word that sounds like viewed, when said aloud

parts.note: eyed means viewed, looked at

explanation.surface: Northerners heard what they saw as a sound policy, far from moderate.
explanation.walkthrough: IDE is said like EYED, meaning viewed. 'Middle-of-the-road' looks political but is literal: the nearside is the kerb side of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: The nearside of a vehicle or road is the side next to the kerb, away from the centre line.

clue.text: One might go into dive with money up front

explanation.surface: Someone dives with money paid in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: A sub is a submarine that dives, and in British usage a sub is an advance on wages.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine plunges under water, and a subsidy or advance is cash paid beforehand.

clue.text: Birds from far away in Crosby causing consternation

indicators.note: in tells us the birds are placed inside the singer's name

parts.note: Bing Crosby was an American crooner
emus are flightless birds from distant Australia

explanation.surface: Exotic birds in the town of Crosby are causing alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosby looks like a place (a town near Liverpool) but it is Bing Crosby.
explanation.definitionFit: Bemusing means puzzling or bewildering, which causes confusion.

clue.text: Asian food gives us hiccups swallowing it

indicators.note: swallowing means the words gives us hiccups hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: Eating Japanese food gives a diner hiccups as they swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is inside 'giveS US HIccups'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with fish.

clue.text: Bashful keeping his head down after the girl finally woke up

indicators.note: after says the shifted his comes after the girl and the final letters

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a girl

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of each of woke and up
head down means the first letter of his is moved to the bottom of this down entry

explanation.surface: The dwarf Bashful keeps his head down after a young woman finally wakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E and P from 'woke up'; 'head down' turns HIS into ISH. Bashful is another of the seven dwarfs, and 'keeping' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheepish means shy and embarrassed, the bashful dwarf's nature.

clue.text: Mix oats with this? Are you sure?

indicators.note: mix tells us to stir the letters of oats and this together

explanation.surface: Someone doubts a recipe telling them to mix oats with this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mix' shuffles OATS and THIS together; 'with' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a spoken expression of doubt or surprise, asking for confirmation.

clue.text: Share out rewritten Q and A, perhaps externally

indicators.note: externally means Q and A are on the outside of the rest
rewritten means the letters of out are written in a new order

explanation.surface: A question-and-answer session is rewritten and shared out.
explanation.walkthrough: Q and A are taken as printed; 'perhaps' suggests a quiz format, not a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A quota is an allotted share or portion.

clue.text: Doc, stuck between queen and king, caught up — not half

indicators.note: stuck between means placed in the gap between the two royal letters
up in a down entry means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
not half means only half of caught is kept, its first three letters

explanation.surface: Doc, one of the seven dwarfs, gets caught between a queen and king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' keeps the first half of caught. Doc is also one of the seven dwarfs.
explanation.definitionFit: Doc is short for doctor, and a quack is slang for a doctor, often an unqualified one.

clue.text: Needing to lose weight, growth is problematic for Grumpy

indicators.note: problematic suggests the letters are in a troubled, disordered state and must be rearranged
needing to lose means letters are taken away

explanation.surface: A dieter's weight-loss struggles make them grumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needing to lose' takes W and T from growth, leaving GROH; 'problematic' rearranges GROH + IS. Grumpy is another dwarf.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogrish means monstrous and bad-tempered, like a fearsome ogre.

clue.text: Sleepy lost with men on manoeuvres

indicators.note: manoeuvres suggests troops shuffled about, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A dwarf is sleepy after losing his way while soldiers are on exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvres' rearranges LOST + MEN ON; 'with' joins them. Sleepy is another of the seven dwarfs.
explanation.definitionFit: Somnolent means drowsy, about to fall asleep.

clue.text: Setter's unfortunately brought up sausage

indicators.note: brought up in a down entry means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the setter speaking says I'm, giving IM
alas is said when something unfortunate happens

explanation.surface: The setter regrets that the sausage they ate came back up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses IM + ALAS, read upwards in the down entry. 'Brought up' looks like vomiting but is the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a spicy cured Italian sausage.

clue.text: Having taken grass and heroin, one may be in court

parts.note: being on drugs means having taken them
oat is a type of grass
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A drug user who has taken grass and heroin may end up in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having taken' looks like part of the drug story but means ON, as in on drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A witness in court swears to tell the truth and so is under a sworn promise.

clue.text: Mister America, love-god, has nothing left

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Mister America, a love god, ends up with nothing left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mister' looks like a title but means a device that mists, a spray.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray can turns liquid into a fine mist, so it is a mist-maker.

clue.text: Miss White's bitten off end of fruit — "you can eat all of it…

definitions.text: you can eat all of it

indicators.note: bitten off end means the final letter is bitten away

parts.note: Snow White is Miss White, so her first name with the possessive gives SNOWS
a pea is botanically a fruit, a seed in a pod

explanation.surface: Snow White bites into the poisoned fruit, as the witch assures her it is all safe to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitten off end' trims SNOWS to SNOW. The surface runs on into 28 across, echoing the witch's apple.
explanation.definitionFit: This pod is a mangetout, French for eat-all, as the whole pod is edible.

clue.text: … it's all right" contrariwise, renders unconscious

indicators.note: contrariwise means the other way round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: it's contains 's, short for is, giving S
OK means all right

explanation.surface: The witch says the apple is safe, but it knocks the princess out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrariwise' reverses S + OK; the clue continues the witch's speech from 27 across.
explanation.definitionFit: KOs are knockouts in boxing, and a knockout leaves the boxer senseless.

clue.text: In case site (no mediation) returns, removes from circulation

indicators.note: returns means the hidden run is read backwards
in tells us the answer sits within the words case site no mediation

explanation.surface: A website returns to service after a dispute without mediation.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters SESITENOMED are inside 'caSE SITE NO MEDiation'; 'returns' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: To demonetise money is to withdraw it as legal tender, taking it out of use.
